text: Paper · arXiv preprint (CC BY 4.0) · arXiv 2611.26172 Budget Internalization: Fixed-Budget RLVR Trades Test-Time Scaling for In-Budget Accuracy Ilia Zavidnyi, Alexander Kovrigin, Arina Puchkova, Kirill Gelvan, Sergey Titov JetBrains Research · 19 November 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version as of 23 November 2026) In one line: On three small models (Qwen3.5-4B, Gemma4-E2B, Nemotron-3-Nano-4B) trained with GRPO on math under a fixed rollout cap (three seeds for the main comparison), AIME accuracy at the cap rose 10.9 to 42.4 points over the base model while accuracy at the largest budget tested fell 13.1 to 30.2 points below it, and none of the tested fixes (single runs on Qwen3.5-4B) kept both the in-budget gain and the base model's test-time scaling. +34.8 / −30.2 points Qwen3.5-4B trained with a 4k-token rollout cap, minus the base model: at a 4k evaluation budget, then at 64k (AIME 2024 and 2025, mean of three seeds) 35.93% against 1.11% at 4k; 48.15% against 78.33% at 64k · §2.1 27.3k → 5.0k tokens per answer mean AIME output length at a 64k budget, base Qwen3.5-4B against its 4k-trained checkpoint; letting it keep thinking ("Wait") adds 2.6k tokens and 0.0 points the cap moved the whole length distribution · Table 1 0 of 11 variants training variants (data, truncation handling, normalisation, KL, supervised controls) that keep a 10-point in-budget gain without falling below the base model at 64k Qwen3.5-4B, 8k cap, one run each · Table 3 How far to trust it: Believe the crossover: it appears in all 18 seeded runs on three model families, the tables reproduce every section 2 number, and the collapse in output length (27.3k to 5.0k tokens for Qwen) explains it.
